courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces concepts of plant growth and development. Covers horticultural practices, crops and environmental factors affecting plant growth.

courses.title: Plant Propagation
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches principles and practices of plant propagation. Examines commercial and home practices. Provides experience in techniques using seed-spores, cuttings, grafting, budding, layering and division.

courses.title: Greenhouse Crop Production I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Covers commercial practices related to production of floriculture crops. Considers production requirements, environmental control and management, and cultural techniques.

courses.title: Greenhouse Crop Production II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Continues commercial practices related to production of floriculture crops. Considers production requirements, environmental control and management, and cultural techniques.

courses.title: Soils
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches theoretical and practical aspects of soils and other growing media. Examines media components, chemical and physical properties, and soil organisms. Discusses management and conservation.

courses.title: Plant Pest Management
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches principles of plant pest management. Covers morphology and life cycles of insects and other small animal pests and plant pathogens. Lab stresses diagnosis, chemical and non-chemical control of specific pests, and pesticide safety.

courses.title: Greenhouse Management
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Discusses the theoretical and applied practices of managing a greenhouse facility. Emphasizes greenhouse construction and design, environmental control, energy conservation, and related topics.

courses.title: Professional Landscape Management
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on basic practices and techniques involving landscape management. Includes development of a year-round management calendar and preparation of bid and contract proposals.

courses.title: Introduction to Floral Design
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches skills required for the composition of basic table arrangements. Includes the history of design styles, identification of flowers and green, identification and use of equipment, and conditioning and handling of flowers.

courses.title: Great Books I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces selected great works of philosophy and literature, with emphasis on close analysis of the text. Part I of II.

courses.title: Introduction to Appalachian Studies
courses.contact_hours: Course Credits 3, Lecture 3
courses.description: Explores the Appalachian region from a cross-disciplinary perspective, with readings on Appalachia drawn primarily from the humanities. Considers the historical, environmental, political and economic contexts that shape Appalachia.

courses.title: Controversial Issues in Contemporary American Culture
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces students to selected issues in contemporary American culture. Includes topic areas ranging from welfare reform, economic development, privacy, environmental protection and conservation, evolution vs. creation, to family values, and special interest lobbying in our state and national governments. Focuses on the development of the student's critical thinking skills by analyzing, evaluating, and reflecting on opposing sides of the same issue as expressed by public leaders, special interest groups and academicians.

courses.title: Early Humanities
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines the values and expression of ideas of selected western and non-western cultures from prehistory up to the 1300s, integrating the arts, literature, religion, and philosophy within the context of history. The assignments in this course require college-level reading, analysis of scholarly studies, and coherent communication through properly cited and formatted written reports. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Modern Humanities
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines the values and expression of ideas of selected western and non-western cultures from the 1300s until 1900s, integrating the visual arts, literature, religion, music and philosophy within the context of history. The assignments in this course require college-level reading, analysis of scholarly studies, and coherent communication through properly cited and formatted written reports. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Introduction to Women and Gender Studies
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Broadens understanding and awareness of women by exploring different cultural, historical, and gendered experiences of social groups throughout the world in relationship to such fields as art, literature, religion, philosophy, social sciences, and music. The assignments in this course require college-level reading, analysis of scholarly studies, and coherent communication through properly cited and formatted written reports. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Introduction to Non-Western Cultures
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces students to beliefs, historical developments, and forms of creative expression that have shaped cultures in regions outside Europe and North America (non-western). Studies the cultures, values, creative expressions, and historical development of selected non-western regions of the world: Asia, Africa, Middle East, Oceania, or the Pre-Columbian Americas. The assignments in this course require college-level reading, analysis of scholarly studies, and coherent communication through properly cited and formatted written reports. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Introduction to African American Studies
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents an interdisciplinary approach to the study of African-American life, history, and culture. Examines specific events, ideologies, and individuals that have shaped the contours of African-American life. Studies the history, sociology, economics, religion, politics, psychology, creative productions, and culture of African- Americans. The assignments in this course require college-level reading, analysis of scholarly studies, and coherent communication through properly cited and formatted written reports. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Interdisciplinary Principles of the Humanities I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Integrates unifying principles of the humanities and related fields of study. Emphasizes the expansion of student's intellectual perspective and development of concepts enabling the integration of knowledge from diverse fields into a unified whole. Part I of II.

courses.title: Interdisciplinary Principles of the Humanities II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Integrates unifying principles of the humanities and related fields of study. Emphasizes the expansion of student's intellectual perspective and development of concepts enabling the integration of knowledge from diverse fields into a unified whole. Part II of II.

courses.title: Comparative Mythology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies the cultural expressions of mythology. Considers selected mythologies representing diverse global culture, with emphasis on parallels and divergences in structure, purpose, and representation in literature and the arts. The assignments in this course require college-level reading, analysis of scholarly studies, and coherent communication through properly cited and formatted written reports. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: The Greek and Roman Tradition
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Explores the significance of Greek and Roman cultures on the individual and society, expressed prominently from the Classical Age in Athens to its survival during Roman times. Examines the key contributions that the Greeks and Romans have imparted upon storytelling, theater, philosophy, civics, political morphology, and the arts and the impact they have in the modern world. The assignments in this course require college-level reading, analysis of scholarly studies, and coherent communication through properly cited and formatted written reports. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Contemporary Humanities
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines selected values and expressions of ideas of western and non-western cultures throughout the twentieth century and beyond, integrating the visual arts, literature, performing arts, religion, and philosophy within the context of history. The assignments in this course require college-level reading, analysis of scholarly studies, and coherent communication through properly cited and formatted written reports

courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies principles and techniques of quality engineering for the management, design engineering economics, production, and assurance of quality. Emphasizes fundamentals of total quality assurance for product and process control. May include design review, fundamentals of statistics procurement control, sampling and control chart systems, quality reporting, process capability analysis, tool and gauge control, document control, or troubleshooting quality control. Part I of II.

courses.title: Industrial Engineering Technology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces basic skills required for a career in industrial engineering technology. Includes basic statistics for engineering technicians, the SI system, graphic analysis, and careers as an industrial engineering technician.

courses.title: Materials and Processes in Manufacturing II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies materials and processes for the manufacture of products. Investigates the nature of various materials. Examines the manufacturing processes of industry and their effects on materials. Part II of II.

courses.title: Materials and Processes of Industry
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies materials and processes for the manufacture of products. Investigates the nature of various materials. Examines the manufacturing processes of industry and their effects on materials.

courses.title: Installation and Preventive Maintenance
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies practices in the installation of machinery, including mounting, grouting, leveling, and alignment. Examines methods of preventive maintenance including inspection, scheduled maintenance, controls, record keeping, repair parts stocking, and safety considerations.

courses.title: Team Concepts & Problem Solving
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies team concepts and problem solving techniques to assist project teams in improving quality and productivity. Provides knowledge of how to work as a team, plan and conduct good meetings, manage logistics and details, gather useful data, communicate the results and implement changes.

courses.title: Quality Control
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies history, structure, and organization of the quality control unit. May include incoming material control, product and process control, and cost control.

courses.title: Statistical Quality Control
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies essentials and application of statistics in quality control function. May include definitions and uses of averages, standard deviations, ranges, and sampling plans. May discuss dependent and independent variables, and distribution probabilities.

courses.title: Industrial Management
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies planning, organizing, directing, and influencing industrial activities. May include research, product design, methods and time management, quality assurance and current manufacturing methodologies.

courses.title: Introduction to Robotics
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 0-2 hours. Total 2-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies evolution and history of robotics with an emphasis on automated and flexible manufacturing. Presents advantages and limitations of present robot systems.

courses.title: World Class Manufacturing I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies the principles and applications of the globalization of industry. Emphasizes the fundamentals of interpersonal/team process, organization skills, total quality tools for continuous improvement, statistical process control, manufacturing resource planning and just- in-time.

courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 4 hours per week. Prerequisite: divisional approval.
courses.description: Introduces terminology and principles related to Mechatronic system design and application. Integrates concepts of electrical/electronic, mechanical and computer technologies in the development, setup, operation and troubleshooting of automated products and systems. Covers breakdown of various automated manufacturing operations with emphasis on system planning, development and troubleshooting processes.

courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-4 hours. Laboratory 0-4 hours. Total 3-6 hours per week. Prerequisite: divisional approval.
courses.description: Presents basic principles used in the design and implementation in manufacturing work cells. Includes selection of the robot system, worksite, application cell sensors, development of cycle times, and economic analysis.

courses.contact_hours: (3 Cr.) Lecture 3 hours, Total 3 hours per week
courses.description: Presents the basic concepts and history of the insurance industry. Includes the types of insurance, how they are regulated, financial performance measures, marketing, underwriting, claims, contracts, property loss exposures, liability loss exposures and risk transfer and management.Examines state's insurance laws and regulations.

courses.title: Personal Insurance
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hour. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents an overview of personal insurance. Emphasis is on automobile, recreational vehicles, homeowners, personal property and personal liability. Provides a comprehensive review of personal insurance issues and planning.

courses.title: Web Page Design I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Stresses a working knowledge of web site designs, construction, and management using HTML or XHTML. Includes headings, lists, links, images, image maps, tables, forms, and frames.

courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Explores the creation of digital graphics for web design. Includes basic design elements such as color and layout will be explored utilizing a computer graphics program(s).

courses.title: Database Fundamentals
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces the student to Relational Database and Relational Database theory. Includes planning, defining and using a database; table design, linking, and normalization; types of databases, database description and definition.

courses.title: Structured Query Language
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Incorporates a working introduction to commands, functions and operators used in SQL for extracting data from standard databases.

courses.title: PL/SQL Programming
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents a working introduction to PL/SQL programming with the Oracle RDBMS environment. Includes PL/SQL fundamentals of block program structure, variables, cursors and exceptions, and creation of program units of procedures, functions, triggers and packages.

courses.title: Database Management Software
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Covers an introduction to relational database theory and how to administer and query databases using multiple commercial database systems.

courses.title: Interactive Web Design
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides techniques in interactive design concepts to create cross-platform, low-bandwidth animations utilizing a vector based application. Emphasizes the importance of usability, accessibility, optimization and performance.

courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Emphasizes techniques to plan and to design a platform- independent commerce Web site. courses.description: Involves in-depth instruction about the underlying architecture of databases and the handling of database administration.

courses.title: Introduction to Information Systems
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Covers the fundamentals of computers and computing and topics which include impact of computers on society, ethical issues, and terminology. Provides discussion about available hardware and software as well as their application.

courses.title: Introduction to Microcomputers
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines concepts and terminology related to microcomputers and introduces specific uses of microcomputers.

courses.title: Computers and Information Systems
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces terminology, concepts, and methods of using computers in information systems. This course teaches computer literacy, not intended for Information Technology majors.

courses.title: Careers and Cyber Ethics
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours per week.
courses.description: Career paths in Information Technology will be explored to help the student determine the appropriate degree plan. Career paths will include but not be limited to software development, computer science, database, networking, system administration and operations, end user support, web design, and management. The student will learn ethical concerns in business and information technology including the ACM Code of Ethics.

courses.title: Introduction to Computer Applications and Concepts
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Covers computer concepts and internet skills, and uses a software suite which includes word processing, spreadsheet, database, and presentation software to demonstrate skills. Recommended prerequisite keyboarding skills. This course applies to career/technical education (CTE) programs. ITE 152 serves both transfer and CTE programs.

courses.title: Survey of Computer Software Applications
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours per week.
courses.description: Review current business software applications for microcomputers emphasizing comparison of a variety of software packages. Provides experience with multiple operating system commands, database, spreadsheet, and word processing programs.

courses.title: Information Literacy
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents the information literacy core competencies focusing on the use of information technology skills. Skills and knowledge will be developed in database searching, computer applications, information security and privacy, and intellectual property issues. This course applies to career/technical education (CTE) programs. ITE 152 serves both transfer and CTE programs.

courses.title: Principles of Information Systems
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides an overview of the fundamentals of computer information systems. Focuses on the role of computers in business today including hardware, software, analysis, design and implementation of information systems. Includes an introduction to computer ethics, and business and personal security. Exposes students to techniques used in programming and system development. Utilizes a hands-on component for spreadsheets, databases, and web design applications.

courses.title: Introduction to Internet Services
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides students with a working knowledge of Internet terminology and services including e-mail, WWW browsing, search engines, ftp, file compression, and other services using a variety of software packages. Provides instruction for basic web page construction.

courses.title: Survey of Internet Services
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces students to basic Internet terminology and services including e-mail, WWW browsing, search engines, ftp telnet, and other services.

courses.title: Artificial Intelligence Awareness
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides instruction in the basics of artificial intelligence (AI) including the complexities of AI, machine and deep learning, and neural networks. Provides students with a clear understanding of history, terminology, concepts, and mechanisms driving AI technologies. Explores how AI is applied in various occupational fields through a blend of theoretical knowledge and case studies.

courses.title: Spreadsheeting for Business
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides a working knowledge of a commercial spreadsheet package to include design and development of a variety of worksheets, preparing graphs, working with database queries, macro writing, menu techniques, and decision analysis tools.

courses.title: Microcomputer Software: Spreadsheets
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides first-time users with sufficient information to make practical use of spreadsheet software using the basic of building spreadsheets.

courses.title: Introduction to Artificial Intelligence Tools for Business
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Explores the applications of artificial intelligence (AI) tools in business. Studies how AI can enhance efficiency, optimize decision-making, and drive innovation in business environments. Includes hands-on projects using AI tools and platforms.

courses.title: Desktop Database Software
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Incorporates instruction in planning, defining, and using a database; performing queries; producing reports; working with multiple files; and concepts of database programming. Includes database concepts, principles of table design and table relationships, entering data, creating and using forms, using data from different sources, filtering, creating mailing labels.

courses.title: Microcomputer Software: Database Management
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents first-time users with sufficient information to make practical use of database management software using the basics of building databases. Covers specific business applications.

courses.title: Introduction to Digital and Information Literacy and Computer Applications
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Develops understanding of digital and information literacy. Introduces basic computer concepts in hardware, software, cyber, cloud, database, and operating systems. Includes hands-on experience developing word processing, spreadsheet and presentation documents. Evaluates the reliability of sources. Covers creating a simple web page. Examines topics such as social, legal, and ethical issues. This is a UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Artificial Intelligence, Ethics and Governance
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Explores ethical considerations surrounding the development, deployment, and use of artificial intelligence (AI) technologies. Examines ethical theories, privacy concerns, biases, human rights implications, transparency challenges, governance frameworks and anticipated ethical issues emerging with advancing AI capabilities. Utilizes case studies to introduce students to ethically responsible practices and strategies for addressing ethical dilemmas in the rapidly evolving field of AI.

courses.title: Multimedia Software
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Explores technical fundamentals of creating multimedia projects with related hardware and software. Students will learn to manage resources required for multimedia production and evaluation and techniques for selection of graphics and multimedia software.

courses.title: Email Essentials
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on providing the student with a working knowledge of introductory email function. Includes the basic concepts of customizing email and using all the email capabilities for reading, creating, sending emails, managing calendar functions and managing contacts, tasks, and notes.

courses.title: Help Desk Support Skills
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Emphasizes instruction in customer support techniques required for analyzing and coordinating software and hardware solutions for end-user needs. includes evaluation and communication techniques required to provide help desk support necessary to transfer knowledge and enable implementation of a solution.

courses.title: User Support/Help Desk Principles
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces a variety of tools and techniques that are used to provide user support in help desk operations. Includes help desk concepts, customer service skills, troubleshooting problems, writing for end users, help desk operations, and software, needs analysis, facilities management, and other related topics related to end user support.

courses.title: Introduction to Telecommunications
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Surveys data transmission systems, communication lines, data sets, network, modes of transmission, protocols, and interfacing. Emphasizes network structure and operation.

courses.title: Introduction to Network Concepts
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides instruction in networking media, physical and logical topologies, common networking standards and popular networking protocols. Emphasizes the TCP/IP protocol suite and related IP addressing schemes, including CIDR. Includes selected topics in network implementation, support and LAN/WAN connectivity.

courses.title: Microcomputer Operating Systems
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches use of operating system utilities and multiple-level directory structures, creation of batch files, and configuration of microcomputer environments. May include a study of graphical user interfaces.

courses.title: Personal Computer Hardware and Troubleshooting
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Includes specially designed instruction to give a student a basic knowledge of hardware and software configurations. Includes the installation of various peripheral devices as well as basic system hardware components.

courses.title: Internet and Network Foundation
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours. Laboratory 0-2 hours. Total 3-5 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides a basic comprehension of Internet and network technologies including IT job roles, connection methods, TCP/IP functionality and DNS. Explores web server technologies with security and project management concepts. Introduces network creation, physical and logical topologies including media properties, server types, IP addressing and network security.

courses.title: Client Operating System (Specify Version)
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Covers installation, configuration, administration, management, maintenance, and troubleshooting of the desktop client operating system in a networked environment.

courses.title: Server Administration (Specify Version)
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Covers installation, configuration, administration, management, maintenance, and troubleshooting of a server in a networked environment.

courses.title: Network Infrastructure (Specify Version)
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Covers planning, installation, configuration, administration, management, maintenance, monitoring, and troubleshooting of network infrastructure components.

courses.title: Active Directory (Specify Version)
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Covers planning, installation, configuration, administration, management, maintenance, monitoring, and troubleshooting of Active Directory (AD) and Domain Name Service (DNS) in a networked environment.

courses.title: Introduction to Networks - Cisco
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 2-3 hours. Total 5-6 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides instruction in the fundamentals of networking environments, the basics of router operations, and basic router and switch configuration.

courses.title: Switching, Routing and Wireless Essentials - Cisco
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 2-3 hours. Total 5-6 hours per week. Prerequisite: ITN 154
courses.description: Provides the skills and knowledge to install, operate, and troubleshoot routers and switches in small networks. Introduces students to wireless local area networks (WLANS) and network security concepts.

courses.title: Enterprise Networking, Security, and Automation - Cisco
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 2-3 hours. Total 5-6 hours per week. Prerequisite: ITN 155
courses.description: Teaches students to configure, troubleshoot, and secure enterprise networks. Introduces students to virtualization, application programming interfaces (APIs) and the configuration management tools that make network automation possible.

courses.title: WAN Technologies - Cisco
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Concentrates on an introduction to Wide Area Networking (WANs). Includes WAN design, LAPB, Frame Relay, ISDN, HDLC, and PPP.

courses.title: Linux System Administration
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses instruction on the installation, configuration and administration of the Linux operating system and emphasizes the use of Linux as a network client and workstation.

courses.title: Unix 1
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides an introduction to UNIX operating systems. Teaches login procedures, file creation, UNIX file structure, input/output control, and the UNIX shell.

courses.title: Administration of Network Resources
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on the management of local area network servers. Teaches proper structuring of security systems. Explains print queues, disk management, and other local area network (LAN) issues. Presents concerns and issues for the purchase and installation of hardware and software upgrades. Can be taught using any network operating system or a range of operating systems as a delivery tool.

courses.title: Protocols and Communications TCP/IP
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Centers on providing an understanding of the TCP/IP suite and the details of its implementation. The details of implementation are treated by discussing IP addressing, the structure of frames and protocol headers that enable communication between two computers. Discusses IP routing, tunneling, SNMP, and security.

courses.title: Voice Over Internet Protocol
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Discusses in depth the concept, theory and principles of Voice over Internet Protocol technology. Reviews the existing PSTN architecture. Examines VOIP Quality of Service, various speech coding techniques, the H.323 architecture, Session Initiation Protocol, Media Gateway Protocol and the relationship between VOIP and SS7.

courses.title: Virtual Infrastructure: Installation and Configuration
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Explores concepts and capabilities of virtual architecture with a focus on the installation, configuration, and management of a virtual infrastructure, and Virtual Center. Covers fundamentals of virtual network design and implementation, fundamentals of storage area networks, virtual switching, virtual system management, and engineering for high availability.

courses.title: Cloud Computing: Infrastructure and Services
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours. Total 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on cloud infrastructure, deployment, security models, and the key considerations in migrating to cloud computing. Covers the technologies and processes required to build traditional, virtualized, and cloud data center environments, including computation, storage, networking, desktop and application virtualization, business continuity, security, and management.

courses.title: Network Security Basics
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides instruction in the basics of network security in depth. Includes security objectives, security architecture, security models and security layers; risk management, network security policy, and security training. Includes the five security keys, confidentiality integrity, availability, accountability and auditability.

courses.title: Network Attacks, Computer Crime and Hacking
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Encompasses in-depth exploration of various methods for attacking and defending a network. Explores network security concepts from the viewpoint hackers and their attack methodologies. Includes topics about hackers, attacks, Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS) malicious code, computer crime and industrial espionage.

courses.title: Network Communication, Security and Authentication
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Covers an in-depth exploration of various communication protocols with a concentration on TCP/IP. Explores communication protocols from the point of view of the hacker in order to highlight protocol weaknesses. Includes Internet architecture, routing, addressing, topology, fragmentation and protocol analysis, and the use of various utilities to explore TCP/IP.

courses.title: Internet/Intranet Firewalls and E-Commerce Security
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Gives an in-depth exploration of firewall, Web security, and e-commerce security. Explores firewall concepts, types, topology and the firewall's relationship to the TCP/IP protocol. Includes client/server architecture, the Web server, HTML and HTTP in relation to Web Security, and digital certification, D.509, and public key infrastructure (PKI).

courses.title: Network Security Layers
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides an in-depth exploration of various security layers needed to protect the network. Explores Network Security from the viewpoint of the environment in which the network operates and the necessity to secure that environment to lower the security risk to the network. Includes physical security, personnel security, operating system security, software security and database security.

courses.title: Legal Topics in Network Security
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours hours per week.
courses.description: Conveys an in-depth exploration of the civil and common law issues that apply to network security. Explores statutes, jurisdictional, and constitutional issues related to computer crimes and privacy. Includes rules of evidence, seizure and evidence handling, court presentation and computer privacy in the digital age.

courses.title: Incident Response and Computer Forensics
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 4-5 hours per week.
courses.description: Prepares the student for a role on an organizational IT support staff where the need for resolving computer incidents is becoming increasingly common. Includes legal and ethical issues of search and seizure of computer and peripheral storage media leading to laboratory exercises examining computers configured with mix of both simulated criminal and other activities which are not criminal in nature, but do violate scenario-driven organizational policy. Requires the student to make choices/recommendations for further pursuit of forensics evidence gathering and analysis. Students will select and gather the utilities and procedures necessary for a court-acceptable forensics toolkit which will then be used to gather and examine specially configured desktop computers. Students will then participate in a mock court proceeding using the collected evidence. Credit will be given to either ITN 275 or ITN 276 and ITN 277 , but not all three courses.

courses.title: Computer Forensics I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week. Prerequisite: ITN 106 , ITN 107 . Co-requisite: ITN 260 .
courses.description: Teaches computer forensic investigation techniques for collecting computer-related evidence at the physical layer from a variety of digital media (hard drives, compact flash and PDAs) and performing analysis at the file system layer. Credit will be given to ITN 275 or ITN 276 and ITN 277 , but not all three courses.

courses.title: C++ Programming I

courses.title: C# Programming I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.

courses.title: Client Side Scripting
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides instruction in fundamentals of Internet application design, development, and deployment using client side scripting language(s).

courses.title: Python Programming
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours. Total 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Entails instruction in fundamentals of object-oriented programming using Python. Emphasizes program construction, algorithm development, coding, debugging, and documentation of Python applications.

courses.title: Introduction to Game Design & Development
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces object-oriented game design and development. Provides overview of the electronic game design and development process and underlines the historical contest, content creation strategies, game careers, and future trends in the industry. Utilizes a game language environment to introduce game design, object-oriented paradigms, software design, software development and product testing. Teaches skills of writing a game design document and creating a game with several levels and objects. Integrate 2D animations, 3D models, sound effects, and background music as well as graphic backgrounds.

courses.title: Gaming and Simulation
courses.description: Introduces students to the concepts and applications of gaming and simulation through the use of gaming and simulation tools, as well as through basic programming skills.

courses.title: Project Management
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces the concepts of project management as defined by the Project Management Institute, the accreditation body for project management.

courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week. 3-4 credits.
courses.description: Provides the necessary design and programming skills required for developing applications on mobile devices (smartphones, tablets, etc.). Utilize the Java-based Android Development Kit to create Android applications, from concept to business model to final product.

courses.title: C++ Programming II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents in-depth instruction of advanced object-oriented techniques for data structures using C++.

courses.title: Server Side Programming
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Centers around instruction in fundamentals of Internet application design, development, and deployment. Includes implementation of server component models, security, and database connectivity using server-side programming.

courses.title: Systems Analysis and Design

courses.description: Focuses on application of information technologies (IT) to system life cycle methodology, systems analysis, systems design, and system implementation practices. courses.title: Introduction to the Law and the Paralegal
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces various areas of law in which a paralegal may be employed. Includes study of the court system (Virginia and federal); a brief overview of criminal law, torts, family law, evidence, the U.C.C., contracts, and ethics; the role of the paralegal; and other areas of interest.

courses.title: Real Estate Law for Legal Assistants
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies law of real property and gives in-depth survey of the more common types of real estate transactions and conveyances such as deeds, contracts, leases, and deeds of trust. Focuses on drafting these various instruments and studies the system of recording and search of public documents.

courses.title: Family Law
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies elements of a valid marriage, grounds for divorce and annulment, separation, defenses, custody, support, adoptions, and applicable tax consequences. Includes property settlement agreements, pre- and ante-nuptial agreements, pleadings, and rules of procedure. May include specific federal and Virginia consumer laws.

courses.title: Legal Research
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides an understanding of various components of a law library, and emphasizes research skills through the use of digests, encyclopedias, reporter systems, codes, citations, ALR, and other research tools. May include research through electronic databases, overview of computer applications, and writing projects.

courses.title: Legal Writing
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week. Prerequisite: ENG 111 or permission of instructor.
courses.description: Studies proper preparation of various legal documents, including legal memoranda, letters, and pleadings. Involves practical applications. May include case and appellate briefs.

courses.title: Legal Research and Writing
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week. Prerequisite: ENG 111 or permission of division.
courses.description: Provides a basic understanding of legal research and the proper preparation of legal documents, including brief writing.

courses.title: Law Office Administration and Management
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces management principles and systems applicable to law firms, including record keeping, disbursements, escrow accounts, billing, and purchasing. May include accounting methods and software packages applicable to law firms.

courses.title: Ethics for the Paralegal
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-3 hours. Total 1-3 hour per week.
courses.description: Examines general principles of ethical conduct applicable to paralegals. Includes the application of rules of ethics to the practicing paralegal.

courses.title: Virginia and Federal Procedure
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines the rules of procedure in the Virginia and federal court systems, including the Federal Rules of Civil Procedure and the Rules of Practice and Procedure in the District Court, Circuit Court, Court of Appeals, and Supreme Court of Virginia.

courses.title: Trial Preparation and Discovery Practice
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines the trial process, including the preparation of a trial notebook, pretrial motions, and orders. May include preparation of interrogatories, depositions, and other discovery tools used in assembling evidence in preparation for the trial or an administrative hearing.

courses.title: Trial Practice and the Law of Evidence
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hour per week.
courses.description: Introduces civil and criminal evidence, including kinds, degrees and admissibility of evidence. Studies methods and techniques of evidence acquisition. Emphasizes Virginia and federal rules of evidence. Focuses on the elements and various problems associated with the trial of a civil or criminal case.

courses.title: Criminal Law
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on major crimes, including their classification, elements of proof, intent, conspiracy, responsibility, parties, and defenses. Emphasizes Virginia law. May include general principles of applicable constitutional law and criminal procedure.

courses.title: Basics of Litigation Support
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides a practical understanding and knowledge of litigation support services, including docket control, case management, document production and organization. Examines the use of privileged documents and various court clerks' offices. Focuses on multiple party case management.

courses.title: Estate Planning and Probate
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces various devices used to plan an estate, including wills, trust, joint ownership and insurance. Considers various plans in light of family situations and estate objectives. Focuses on practices involving administration of an estate including taxes and preparation of forms.

courses.title: Real Estate Abstracting
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Reviews aspects of abstracting title to real estate, recordation of land transactions, liens, grantor-grantee indices, warranties, covenants, restrictions, and easements.

courses.title: Legal Transactions
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents an in-depth study of general contract law, including formation, breach, enforcement, and remedies. May include an overview of UCC sales, commercial paper, and collections.

courses.title: Bankruptcy
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides a practical understanding of non-bankruptcy alternatives and the laws of bankruptcy including Chapters 7, 11, 12 and 13 of the Bankruptcy Code. Emphasizes will be placed on preparing petitions, schedules, statements, and other forms.

courses.title: Coordinated Internship
courses.contact_hours: Credit/practice ratio not to exceed 1:5 hours. May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Supervises on-the-job training in selected business, industrial or service firms coordinated by the college.

courses.title: Seminar and Project
courses.contact_hours: May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Requires completion of a project or research report related to the student's occupational objectives and a study of approaches to the selection and pursuit of career opportunities in the field.

courses.title: Machine Shop I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 4-5 hours. Laboratory 9 hours. Total 13-14 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces the machinist to identification, care, and use of precision tools and instruments. Emphasizes the operation of the drill press, lathe, power saw, grinder, and milling machine. Covers the sharpening of lathe curing tools, safety, and good housekeeping. Provides for operation and setup on the various types of precision grinders, milling machines, and drill presses. Part I of II.

courses.title: Machine Shop II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 4-5 hours. Laboratory 9 hours. Total 13-14 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces the machinist to identification, care, and use of precision tools and instruments. Emphasizes the operation of the drill press, lathe, power saw, grinder, and milling machine. Covers the sharpening of lathe curing tools, safety, and good housekeeping. Provides for operation and setup on the various types of precision grinders, milling machines, and drill presses. Part II of II.

courses.title: Machine Shop Operations
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours. Laboratory 15 hours. Total 18-19 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces bench work, sawing, drilling, lathe, milling, grinding, precision instruments, and safety. Requires solutions of related problems and preparation of weekly laboratory reports.

courses.title: Technology of Machining
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours. Laboratory 15 hours. Total 18-19 hours per week.
courses.description: Offers practice in bench work, sawing, drilling, lathe, milling, grinding, and precision measuring instruments. May require solutions of related problems and preparation of weekly laboratory reports.

courses.title: Machine Trade Theory and Computation I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Covers shop theory and mathematics dealing with fractional and precision measuring tools. Includes layout, bandsaws, drill presses, the twist drill, thread cutting, taper turning, vertical and horizontal milling machines, lathe tool bit geometry, the engine lathe, and other lathe operations. Part I of II.

courses.title: Machinist Handbook
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours per week.
courses.description: Uses the machinist handbook as a ready reference book of tabular data, formulas, designs and processes relating to machine technology.

courses.title: Numerical Control I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours. Laboratory 2-3 hours. Total 3-5 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on numerical control techniques in metal forming and machine processes. Includes theory and practice in lathe and milling machine computer numerical control program writing, setup and operation. Part I of II.

courses.title: Numerical Control II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours. Laboratory 2-3 hours. Total 3-5 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on numerical control techniques in metal forming and machine processes. Includes theory and practice in lathe and milling machine computer numerical control program writing, setup and operation. Part II of II.

courses.title: Computer Numerical Control III
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours. Laboratory 2-3 hours. Total 3-5 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on numerical control techniques in metal forming and machine processes. Includes theory and practice in lathe and milling machine computer numerical control program writing, setup and operation.

courses.title: Introduction to Geometrical Dimensioning and Tolerancing in Machining
courses.contact_hours: Lecture hours 3 per week.
courses.description: Focuses on basic topics in geometrical dimensioning and tolerancing (GD&T). Covers internationally recognized GD&T symbols. Explains the importance of a feature control frame. Teaches the Cartesian coordinate system in relation to precision components. Examines theoretical and practical concepts of geometric controls relative to design, tooling, production, and inspection.

courses.title: Introductory CNC Programming
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces programming of computerized numerical control machines with hands-on programming and operation of CNC machines.

courses.title: Advanced CNC Programming
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides in-depth study of programming computerized numerical control machines.

courses.title: CNC Programming
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches programming of computerized numerical control machines. Focuses on CNC machining processes.

courses.title: Metals/Heat Treatment
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides approach to metals and their structure. Gives working knowledge of methods of treating ferrous and non- ferrous metals.

courses.title: Introduction to Computer Aided Manufacturing
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours. Laboratory 2-4 hours. Total 3-6 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces computer aided manufacturing (CAM) with emphasis on programming of numerical control machinery. Teaches program writing procedures using proper language and logic and a CAM programming system to produce numerical control code for machines. Teaches basic computer usage, 2 1/2D and 3D CAD-CAM integration, and code-to-machine transfer.

courses.title: Machine Tool Maintenance
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces tool design from a maintenance and repair standpoint. Emphasizes proper care, repair, and preventative maintenance of machine tools.

courses.title: Machine Shop Practices I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 2-3 hours. Total 4-5 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces safety procedures, bench work, hand tools, precision measuring instruments, drill presses, cut-off saws, engine lathes, manual surface grinders, and milling machines. Part I of II.

courses.title: Machine Shop Practices II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 2-3 hours. Total 4-5 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces safety procedures, bench work, hand tools, precision measuring instruments, drill presses, cut-off saws, engine lathes, manual surface grinders, and milling machines. Part II of II.

courses.title: Machine Shop Practices III
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Offers practice in the operation of the drill press, engine lathe, vertical milling machine, horizontal milling machine, and the surface grinder. Introduces practical heat treatment of directly hardenable steels commonly used in machine shops. Part I of II.

courses.title: Machine Shop Practices IV
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Offers practice in the operation of the drill press, engine lathe, vertical milling machine, horizontal milling machine, and the surface grinder. Introduces practical heat treatment of directly hardenable steels commonly used in machine shops. Part II of II.

courses.title: Machine Blueprint Reading I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces reading and interpreting blueprints and working drawings. Applies visualization of objects, sketching, and machine terminology. Part I of II.

courses.title: Machine Blueprint Reading II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces reading and interpreting blueprints and working drawings. Applies visualization of objects, sketching, and machine terminology. Part II of II.

courses.title: Topics In
courses.contact_hours: May be used also for special honors courses. May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Provides an opportunity to explore topical areas of interest to or needed by students.

courses.title: Cooperative Education
courses.contact_hours: Credit/work ratio not to exceed 1:5 hours. May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Supervises in on-the-job training for pay in approved business, industrial and service firms, coordinated by the college's cooperative education office. Is applicable to all occupational- technical curricula at the discretion of the college.

courses.title: Seminar and Project
courses.contact_hours: May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Requires completion of a project or research report related to the student's occupational objectives and a study of approaches to the selection and pursuit of career opportunities in the field.

courses.title: Supervised Study
courses.contact_hours: May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Assigns problems for independent study incorporating previous instruction and supervised by the instructor.

courses.title: Production Machining Techniques
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 4 hours. Laboratory 6 hours. Total 10 hours per week.
courses.description: Offers practice in advanced machine shop. Emphasizes mass production techniques and interchangeable parts manufacture. Covers setup and operation of tooling and fixtures to manufacture work pieces to specified tolerances.

courses.title: Standards, Measurements and Calculations
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents typical mathematical and mechanical problems requiring the use of reference standards such as the Machinery's Handbook for solution. Presents use of the Coordinate Measuring Machine for solution.

courses.title: Advanced Machine Tool Operations I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 4 hours. Laboratory 9 hours. Total 13 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on advanced lathe and mill work with concentration on fits, finishes, inspection, quality control, and basic heat treating. Includes design and construction of specific projects to determine the student's operational knowledge of all equipment. Part I of II.

courses.title: Advanced Machine Tool Operations II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 4 hours. Laboratory 9 hours. Total 13 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on advanced lathe and mill work with concentration on fits, finishes, inspection, quality control, and basic heat treating. Includes design and construction of specific projects to determine the student's operational knowledge of all equipment. Part II of II.

courses.title: Advanced Machine Tool Operations III
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 4 hours. Laboratory 9 hours. Total 13 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches precision grinding, grinding allowances, and electro- discharge machining.

courses.title: Advanced Precision Machining I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches machining principles and calculations necessary for the precision required by the machinist. Emphasizes advanced lathe and mill work with concentration of fits. finishes, inspection, and quality control. Includes design and construction of specific projects to determine the student's operational knowledge of all equipment. Part I of II.

courses.title: Advanced Precision Machining II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches machining principles and calculations necessary for the precision required by the machinist. Emphasizes advanced lathe and mill work with concentration of fits. finishes, inspection, and quality control. Includes design and construction of specific projects to determine the student's operational knowledge of all equipment. Part II of II.

courses.title: Advanced Machinery Procedures I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on machining principles and calculations necessary for the precision required by the machinist. Emphasizes advanced lathe and mill work with concentration on fits, finishes, inspections, and quality control. Teaches design and construction of specific projects to determine the student's operational knowledge of all equipment. Part I of II.

courses.title: Advanced Machinery Procedures II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on machining principles and calculations necessary for the precision required by the machinist. Emphasizes advanced lathe and mill work with concentration on fits, finishes, inspections, and quality control. Teaches design and construction of specific projects to determine the student's operational knowledge of all equipment. Part II of II.

courses.title: Introduction to Supply Chain Strategies for Industry
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour, Laboratory 6 hours, Total 7 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on effective supply chain strategies for industry. Covers first article part inspections and production validation. Demonstrates flow cell ideology in a live flow cell production environment. Examines value stream mapping, customer/supplier roles, and quality systems in addition to proper health and safety guidelines.

courses.title: Introduction to Algebra
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Covers topics in arithmetic through introduction to variables and equations.

courses.title: Learning Support for Quantitative Reasoning
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week. Corequisite: MTH 154
courses.description: Provides support to ensure success for students co-enrolled in Quantitative Reasoning (MTH 154). Course will review foundational topics through direct instruction, guided practice, and individualized support.

courses.title: Learning Support for Statistical Reasoning
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 credits. Total 3 hours per week. Corequisite: MTH 155
courses.description: Provides support to ensure success for students co-enrolled in Statistical Reasoning (MTH 155). Course will review foundational topics through direct instruction, guided practice, and individualized support.

courses.title: Intermediate Algebra
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Covers topics in algebra.

courses.title: Learning Support for Pre-Calculus
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week. Corequisite: MTH 161
courses.description: Provides support to ensure success for students co-enrolled in Pre-Calculus (MTH 161). Course will review foundational topics through direct instruction, guided practice, and individualized support.

courses.title: Introduction to Medical Laboratory Technology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces the basic principles, techniques, and vocabulary applicable to all phases of medical laboratory technology.

courses.title: Introduction to Medical Laboratory Techniques
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces the basic techniques including design of the health care system, ethics, terminology, calculations, venipuncture and routine urinalysis.

courses.title: Phlebotomy
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3-6 hours. Total 5-8 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces basic medical terminology, anatomy, physiology, components of health care delivery and clinical laboratory structure. Teaches techniques of specimen collection, specimen handling, and patient interactions.

courses.title: Clinical Phlebotomy
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 6 hours. Total 8 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on obtaining blood specimens, processing specimens, managing assignments, assisting with and/or performing specified tests, performing clerical duties and maintaining professional communication. Provides supervised learning in college laboratory/and or cooperating agencies.

courses.title: Clinical Immunohematology/Immunology I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 6 hours. Total 8 hours per week.
courses.description: Incorporates basic principles of antigen and antibody reactions included in blood grouping and typing, compatibility testing, and serological procedure.

courses.title: Hematology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour. Laboratory 6 hours. Total 7 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches various blood components, how they are obtained and methods of examination. Includes erythrocyte, leukocyte and platelet counts, hemoglobin and hematocrit determinations, normal and abnormal smears. Introduces coagulation screening studies.

courses.title: Basic Clinical Microbiology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies classification, theories, techniques, and methods used in basic bacteriology, parasitology, and mycology. Emphasizes routine identification.

courses.title: Clinical Urinalysis
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour. Laboratory 3 hour. Total 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on urinalysis studies including physical and chemical properties, microscopic techniques. Emphasizes the significance of abnormal results.

courses.contact_hours: Credit/practice ratio not to exceed 1:5 hours. May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.

courses.description: Requires completion of a project or research report related to the student's occupational objectives and a study of approaches to the selection and pursuit of career opportunities in the field.

courses.title: Clinical Hematology II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3-6 hours. Total 5-8 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches advanced study of blood to include coagulation, abnormal bloody formation, and changes seen in various diseases.

courses.title: Clinical Immunohematology/Immunology II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour. Laboratory 6 hours. Total 7 hours per week.
courses.description: Emphasizes ability to apply theories and procedures utilized in immunohematology for routine transfusion and donor services. Correlates theories with practical application in order to assess cellular and immune mechanisms in specific disease states.

courses.title: Clinical Microscopy
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 4-5 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies theories, principles, and interpretation of test results for urine and body fluids associated with normal and abnormal states.

courses.title: Clinical Microbiology II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours. Laboratory 3-6 hours. Total 4-8 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches handling, isolation, and identification of pathogenic microorganisms. Emphasizes clinical techniques of bacteriology, mycology, parasitology and virology. Part II of II.

courses.title: Clinical Chemistry and Instrumentation I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 3-6 hours. Total 6-9 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces methods of performing biochemical analysis of clinical specimens. Teaches instrumentation involved in a clinical chemistry laboratory, quality control, and the ability to recognize technical problems. Part I of II.

courses.title: Clinical Chemistry and Instrumentation II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 3-6 hours. Total 6-9 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces methods of performing biochemical analysis of clinical specimens. Teaches instrumentation involved in a clinical chemistry laboratory, quality control, and the ability to recognize technical problems. Part II of II.

courses.title: Clinical Chemistry and Instrumentation III
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours. Laboratory 3-6 hours. Total 5-8 hours per week.
courses.description: Emphasizes application of chemical theories and principles to perform routines and special chemistries on various types of instrumentations, to evaluate quality control programs, and to associate test results with clinical significance.

courses.title: Clinical Hematology III
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours. Laboratory 3-6 hours. Total 5-8 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on maintenance and troubleshooting of automated equipment, on evaluation of quality control programs, on blood dyscrasias, utilizing special stains and bone marrow studies, and on specialized studies for evaluating problems of hemostasis.

courses.title: Clinical Microbiology III
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 4-5 hours per week.
courses.description: Stresses ability of the student to culture and identify pathogenic and non-pathogenic bacterial and mycotic agents, to identify parasites, and to associate microorganisms with clinical symptoms.

courses.title: Coordinated Internship
courses.contact_hours: Credit/practice ratio not to exceed 1:5 hours. May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Supervises on-the-job training in selected business, industrial or service firms coordinated by the college.

courses.title: Seminar and Project
courses.contact_hours: May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Requires completion of a project or research report related to the student's occupational objectives and a study of approaches to the selection and pursuit of career opportunities in the field.

courses.title: Supervised Study
courses.contact_hours: May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Assigns problems for independent study incorporating previous instruction and supervised by the instructor.

courses.title: Introduction to Engineering Technology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces professional fields of engineering technology. Covers the work of the engineering technologist, professional ethics, division of industrial practice, and engineering problem solving with hand calculator and computer applications.

courses.title: Introduction to Engineering Technology I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces engineering technology. Provides historical background. Covers such topics as professional ethics; problem solving techniques involving forces, structures, materials, fluids, energy, and electricity and U.S. Customary and S.I. units, and unit conversions. Part I of II.

courses.title: Introduction to Engineering Technology II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces engineering technology. Provides historical background. Covers such topics as professional ethics; problem solving techniques involving forces, structures, materials, fluids, energy, and electricity and U.S. Customary and S.I. units, and unit conversions. Part II of II.

courses.title: Electronic Circuits and Instrumentation
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 6 hours per week.
courses.description: Designed for non-majors. Covers electronic circuits, devices, instrumentation and basic communications, DC and AC theory, introduction to power supplies, amplifiers, and measurement devices.

courses.title: Materials and Processes of Industry
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies engineering materials and accompanying industrial manufacturing processes. Investigates nature of materials structure and properties from a design standpoint. Analyzes the effects of various processes on materials, and the processes themselves. Includes machining, casting, forming, molding, hot/cold working, cipless machining, and welding. Addresses quality assurance and inspection procedures.

courses.title: Introduction to Basic CNC and CAM
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours. Laboratory 2-4 hours. Total 3-5 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches the basic concepts of Computer Numerical Control (CNC) programming of Numerical Control Machinery with emphasis on Computer Aided Manufacturing (CAM)/Computer Aided Drafting (CAD). Program writing procedures will be based on using the following: basic G-code programming language for CNC machinery, CAD/CAM programming systems to produce correct code for CNC Machinery, basic computer usage, CAD/CAM integration, and Code-to-machine transfer via Distributive Numeric Control (DNC).

courses.title: 3D Printing for Engineering Design
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours, Laboratory 3 hours, Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides an overview of rapid technologies in Additive Manufacturing that are high productivity tools designed to cut lead times, reduce time to market, increase the quality of the product, and improve collaboration within the organization.

courses.title: Mechanics I - Statics for Engineering Technology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches Newton's laws, resultants and equilibrium of force systems, trusses and frames, determination of centroids, and distributed loads and moments of inertia. Introduces dry friction and force systems in space.

courses.title: Introduction to Mechatronics
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents foundational concepts in mechatronics including analog and digital electronics, sensors, actuators, microprocessors, and microprocessor interfacing to electromechanical systems. Surveys components and measurement equipment used in the design, installation, and repair of mechatronic equipment and circuits. This course is cross-listed with ETR 140 . Credit will not be awarded for both.

courses.title: Mechanisms
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours. Laboratory 2-4 hours. Total 3-5 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies the purpose and actions of cams, gear trains, levers, and other mechanical devices used to transmit control. Focuses on motions, linkages, velocities, and acceleration of points within a link mechanism; layout method for designing cams and gear grain. Requires preparation of weekly laboratory reports.

courses.title: Basic Fluid Mechanics - Hydraulics/Pneumatics
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 2-3 hours. Total 4-6 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces theory, operation and maintenance of hydraulic/ pneumatics devices and systems. Emphasizes the properties of fluids, fluid flow, fluid statics, and the application of Bernoulli's equation.

courses.title: Applied Hydraulics and Pneumatics
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-3 hours. Laboratory 1-3 hours. Total 2-5 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces hydraulic and pneumatic systems found in construction equipment, road vehicles, and farm equipment. Includes the basic theory, construction, maintenance and repair of hydraulic and pneumatic power systems.

courses.title: Applied Hydraulics, Pneumatics and Hydrostatics
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches fluid power system design, operation, testing, maintenance and repair. Includes reservoirs, pump connecting valves, cylinders, pressure regulating valves, flow control valves, hydraulic motors, and introduction to basic hydrostatic hydraulic systems.

courses.title: Topics In
courses.contact_hours: May be used also for special honors courses. May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Provides an opportunity to explore topical areas of interest to or needed by students.

courses.title: Mechatronic Process Control
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 4 hours per week. Prerequisite: MEC 140 or divisional approval.
courses.description: Studies systems integrating mechanical components with electrical components and logic devices used to control manufacturing operations. Surveys electromechanical actuators, sensors, digital to analog conversion, and methods of computer control as related to the managing and monitoring of manufacturing processes.

courses.title: Applications of Fluid Mechanics
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches theory of hydraulic and pneumatic circuits including motors, controls, actuators, valves, plumbing, accumulators, reservoirs, pumps, compressors, and filters.

courses.title: Supervised Study
courses.contact_hours: May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Assigns problems for independent study incorporating previous instruction and supervised by the instructor.

courses.title: Introduction to Mental Health
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Surveys history of mental health from ancient to contemporary times, with special emphasis on impact of the Psychoanalytic, Humanistic, and Behavioral movements in the treatment of mental illness. Includes examination of structure and functions of human service delivery systems, knowledge and skills of mental health workers, and current ethical and legal issues.

courses.title: Mental Health Skill Training I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Develops skills necessary to function as a mental health worker, with emphasis on guided practice in counseling skills as well as improved self-awareness. Includes training in problem-solving, goal-setting, and implementation of appropriate strategies and evaluation techniques relating to interaction involving a variety of client needs. Part I of II.

courses.title: Mental Health Skill Training II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Develops skills necessary to function as a mental health worker, with emphasis on guided practice in counseling skills as well as improved self-awareness. Includes training in problem-solving, goal-setting, and implementation of appropriate strategies and evaluation techniques relating to interaction involving a variety of client needs. Part II of II.

courses.title: Introduction to Abnormal Psychology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies symptoms, causes and treatment of mental deficiency, neurosis, psychosis and character disorders, with specific relationship to work of the mental health technologists.

courses.title: Coordinated Internship
courses.contact_hours: Credit/practice ratio not to exceed 1:5 hours. May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Supervises on-the-job training in selected business, industrial or service firms coordinated by the college.

courses.description: Studies various models of counseling theories and appropriate application of counseling techniques in the helping profession.
